sources.title: FishBase: Lutjanus griseus

sources.title: FishBase: Gerres cinereus
sources.supports: shallow sandy areas, seagrass and mangrove channels; eats benthic invertebrates

sources.title: FishBase: Lutjanus apodus
sources.supports: clear shallow reef water, juveniles over seagrass and mangrove mud; rests in groups by day

sources.title: Ecosphere (2018): acoustic telemetry of schoolmaster snapper and great barracuda
sources.supports: phase: schoolmaster hold at mangrove prop roots by day and leave them for edges, channels and seagrass at night (abstract via search)

designNotes: Rests here by day and leaves to feed over sand and seagrass at night, so it is met mostly in daylight here and at night in channels and grass beds.

sources.title: Florida Museum species profile: Centropomus undecimalis
sources.supports: mangroves, beaches and river mouths; cold limits of 6 to 12 °C for adults

sources.title: Salt Water Sportsman: sundown snook
sources.supports: phase: snook hold in the shadows around dock lights and along bridge shadow lines at night (Florida)

sources.title: Belize snook seasons (several guide pages)
sources.supports: months: Belize guides disagree (summer; November to April; December to March), so the game keeps snook level all year; Belize water never reaches the cold limit

sources.title: FishBase: Sphyraena barracuda

sources.title: FishingBooker: great barracuda fishing in Placencia, Belize

sources.title: Florida Museum species profile: Megalops atlanticus

designNotes: Rare rather than epic here: creek tarpon are the first ones a shop rod can turn.
